extraneous

/ik-STRAY-nee-uhs/ - the stress falls on STRAY · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Extraneous means irrelevant, extra, not necessary.

Log only the pendulum's swing time, the lab sheet warns; the color of the string is extraneous data.

Worked Example

The volcano-acidity poster lost points for its extraneous panels: a timeline of the student's pets, a photo of the family dog wearing safety goggles, and a paragraph on favorite lunches. Charming, every one — and none of it had anything to do with volcanoes.

Extraneous is the precise word because the material comes from outside the subject. The dog photo isn't wrong, sloppy, or false; it simply doesn't belong to the matter at hand. Extraneous marks that outsider status — imported material a subject never asked for.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

irrelevant: Irrelevant judges a thing against the question at hand: whatever it is and wherever it came from, it fails to bear on the point. Extraneous adds a story about origin — the material walked in from outside the subject entirely. A detail can be irrelevant while still belonging to the file; extraneous detail never belonged.

unrelated: Unrelated is the total break: the thing has no connection to the matter at all, near or far. Extraneous is softer and more particular — extraneous material can touch the subject and still not belong, because it was imported from somewhere else. Everything unrelated is extraneous; not the reverse.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

pertinent: bearing directly on the matter

germane: belonging naturally to the discussion at hand

Where it sits · how little it belongs to the matter — unneeded → extraneous → distracting

unneeded vs. extraneous: An unneeded detail merely fails to help; an extraneous one comes from outside the subject entirely — it was never part of the matter to begin with.

distracting vs. extraneous: Distracting sits a rung past extraneous: the imported material has stopped being harmless and started pulling attention away from the point.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — extra-

Prefix — extra-: outside, beyond

Suffix — -neous

Suffix — -neous: adjective-forming (Latin -neus)

Put it together

Put it together: Extra- (outside, beyond) + -neous (adjective-forming) = from the outside. Latin extraneus meant 'external, foreign' — and through Old French the very same word wore down into English strange. Extraneous material is, quite exactly, the stranger in the room: it drifted in from outside the subject.

Use the root in a new word: extraterrestrial

Use the root in a new word: extraterrestrial: Astronomers listen for radio signals that might carry an extraterrestrial hello from beyond Earth.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / academic

Extraneous and superfluous — a unit-mate — divide the territory of 'too much.' Extraneous material comes from outside the subject: the pet timeline on a volcano poster. Superfluous material belongs in kind but exceeds the need: the fourth example proving a point the first three settled. Off-topic, reach for extraneous; on-topic but past need, superfluous.
